brief_answers.treatability: Atopic dermatitis can be treated to control symptoms and flare-ups. A dermatologist can help choose a treatment plan.
brief_answers.curability: Atopic dermatitis has no current cure, but treatment can control it. Improvement does not necessarily mean it will never flare again.

self_care: Use a gentle, fragrance-free moisturizer and cleanser; be gentle when bathing.
Identify and avoid personal flare triggers, such as irritating products or fabrics.
clinician_options: A clinician may prescribe topical corticosteroids or non-steroid anti-inflammatory creams, such as topical calcineurin inhibitors.
More difficult cases may need supervised light therapy or systemic treatment.
atopic_dermatitis.seek_care: Arrange an assessment for persistent or difficult-to-control symptoms. The treatment choice depends on age, body area, severity, and medical history.

brief_answers.treatability: Contact dermatitis can be treated. Identifying and avoiding the substance causing it is a key part of care.
brief_answers.curability: Contact dermatitis can clear when its cause is identified and avoided. It can recur with further exposure, so finding the trigger matters.

self_care: Avoid the suspected substance touching your skin; a clinician can help identify the trigger.
A cool, damp compress can help ease itching.
clinician_options: A clinician may prescribe a topical corticosteroid to reduce inflammation, with the strength chosen for the body area and severity.
Patch testing may help identify an allergy; extensive or persistent reactions may need other clinician-supervised treatment.
contact_dermatitis.seek_care: Seek an assessment if the trigger is unclear, the rash keeps returning, or symptoms are extensive or worsening.

brief_answers.treatability: Lichen planus has treatments that can relieve symptoms or prevent worsening. Some mild skin cases improve without treatment; care depends on the affected area.
brief_answers.curability: Lichen planus has no current cure, although it can go away on its own for some people. Treatment can help prevent worsening.

self_care: Use gentle, fragrance-free skin care and avoid rubbing or scratching affected skin.
A cool compress may ease itching.
clinician_options: Some mild skin cases need monitoring rather than medication; a clinician should confirm this.
Treatment may include topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, or medicine for itching; more extensive skin disease may need light therapy or systemic treatment.
lichen_planus.seek_care: Arrange a dermatology assessment. Mouth, genital, scalp, or nail involvement needs care tailored to that site; a skin photo cannot determine that treatment.

brief_answers.treatability: Psoriasis can be treated to reduce symptoms and control flare-ups. The appropriate treatment depends on its type, extent, and severity.
brief_answers.curability: Psoriasis has no current cure, but treatments can help control it and improve symptoms.

self_care: Follow gentle skin care and use moisturizer to help manage dry skin.
Identify personal triggers and avoid scratching or picking the affected skin.
clinician_options: A dermatologist may prescribe topical corticosteroids, vitamin D analogues, or other topical medicines.
More extensive disease may need supervised phototherapy or systemic medicines, including biologics. Do not use tanning beds as treatment.
psoriasis.seek_care: A dermatologist should confirm the diagnosis and choose treatment for the affected area and severity. Mention joint pain, stiffness, or swelling during your assessment.

rosacea.nonfacial_site_note: Rosacea mainly affects the face. A concern on the buttocks needs assessment; I cannot assume rosacea is its cause.

brief_answers.treatability: Rosacea treatment can help control symptoms and reduce flare-ups. A dermatologist can help choose care for the particular signs you have.
brief_answers.curability: Rosacea has no current cure, but treatment can help control its symptoms and flare-ups.

self_care: Use a gentle cleanser, moisturizer, and broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher.
Identify and limit personal flare triggers, such as overheating or irritating skin products.
clinician_options: A dermatologist may prescribe topical medicines such as azelaic acid, metronidazole, or ivermectin for acne-like bumps.
Some cases need oral medicine or laser/light treatment, depending on the signs and medical history.
rosacea.seek_care: Arrange an assessment to confirm rosacea. Eye irritation needs clinician evaluation; eye pain or changes in vision require prompt medical care.

brief_answers.treatability: Dermatitis has treatment options. The right approach depends on the type, such as atopic or contact dermatitis; that type has not been confirmed here.
brief_answers.curability: Whether dermatitis clears or needs ongoing control depends on its type and cause. Atopic dermatitis has no current cure; contact dermatitis can clear when the trigger is avoided.

self_care: Use gentle, fragrance-free skin care and avoid products that irritate the affected skin.
clinician_options: A clinician needs to identify the type of dermatitis before selecting medication; atopic and contact dermatitis can need different plans.
dermatitis.seek_care: Ask a dermatologist to confirm the type and cause, especially when symptoms persist or worsen.

brief_answers.treatability: Hives can be treated to reduce itching and new outbreaks. Many cases settle, while recurring or long-lasting hives may need a clinician's treatment plan.
brief_answers.curability: Hives can settle, but recurring or long-lasting hives need assessment. The outlook depends on the type and cause.

self_care: Avoid known triggers and use gentle skin care; recurrent hives should be assessed.
clinician_options: A clinician or pharmacist can assess whether an oral antihistamine is appropriate; persistent hives may need specialist treatment.
hives.seek_care: Seek emergency care for trouble breathing or swallowing, faintness, or swelling of the face, mouth, or throat. Hives are an information topic, not one of this photo model's supported classes.

self_care: General skin care can include gentle cleansing, moisturizer when needed, and sun protection.
normal_skin.seek_care: No disease-specific medication can be selected from this label. A normal-skin match does not prove healthy skin; persistent or worsening symptoms should be assessed.
